answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent's history to a succinct ZK-STARK proof, while a verifiable delay function forces a deterministic time-lock that any Sybil clone must recompute, making forging cost exponential in stake. A minimum collateral of 10^4 tokens is slashed on any deviation, yielding negative expected attack utility and a robust Nash equilibrium. The ember of each proof, the pearl of accumulated reputation, and the kernel of the delay circuit together form an information-theoretic barrier against cloning.
